scenario: A true-wireless-earbud buyer wants to know whether a roughly $30-to-$300 budget contains a defensible sound-quality cutoff. The buyer's brother uses inexpensive earbuds, a friend uses a pair said to cost about $280, and a casual comparison on a bus did not reveal an obvious difference. Four saved listings are available: YOVDA K98 at $29.99, generic F9 TWS at $43.28, an Avantree DG45 plus TWS120 aptX bundle at $59.99, and KW-01 at $139.90. There is no eligible saved $200-to-$300 true-wireless listing. The buyer asks whether the available evidence supports a broad diminishing-returns boundary or a product choice, and whether an advertised codec should affect value. The exact phone or computer, operating system, active codec and configuration, listening level, content, fit, quiet-room result, current seller, return window, and matched cross-tier result are not yet known.
constraints: The available listings stop at $139.90 and do not cover the $200-to-$300 tier.
Seller prices and feature descriptions are not independent listening tests.
Price alone cannot establish audible quality.
The Avantree price includes a Windows USB adapter as well as earbuds.
No posted review score is not a zero-star result.
Codec value depends on the buyer's actual playback configuration.
A codec comparison must match content, level, conditions, and bitrate where applicable.
The bus anecdote is uncontrolled and may be affected by masking.
A single owner discussion cannot establish a population cutoff.
A cutoff or winner needs matched evidence across eligible returnable tiers.
target: Compare the four saved listings and determine whether the available product, codec-method, masking, and owner-context material supports a broad $30-to-$300 sound-quality cutoff or a product choice. Preserve the limits of seller descriptions, prices, missing reviews, bundle contents, missing upper-tier coverage, codec configuration, listening method, and the bus comparison. If the material is insufficient, explain why and give a practical matched returnable trial with a clear end point.
